note: Plan-only prompt on a fresh claude-opus-5-5 subagent; control without the skill. Evidence: in a real session three PRs adding rows to the same README and AGENTS.md tables conflicted twice in a row, because each merge broke the next. For changelog-duplicate and failed-check-under-load, the requester supplied measured runs from 2026-10-12 on claude-opus-5-5: the leading, plan-only prompts used fresh claude -p sessions in empty scratch directories with read-only tools. The realistic changelog pair used fresh claude -p sessions in a real git repo with full tool access. Each pair used an unchanged prompt. Control used landing-parallel-prs from origin/main; revised used this branch before the review fixes. These results do not measure the final review fixes.

evals.prompt: PRs #21, #22 and #23 each add one row to the skills table in README.md and AGENTS.md. All three are approved by review. Land all three. Give the exact commands in order; do not run them.
evals.expected_output: merges one PR at a time; before each next merge, merges origin/main into that branch keeping both rows, pushes normally, waits with a deadline for checks on the new head SHA, asks the user's OK before each merge
assertions: no rebase and no force-push
updates each PR from main right before its own merge, not all three up front
asks for the user's explicit OK before each gh pr merge
waits for checks with a timeout on the new head SHA
each gh pr merge carries --match-head-commit with the approved and checked SHA
waits for state MERGED with a deadline before updating the next PR
the MERGEABLE wait has a limit and stops on CONFLICTING or timeout
baseline_failures: control rebased #22 and #23 onto main and pushed with --force-with-lease
control merged each PR right after checks, with no user OK per merge
evals.with_skill_result: 2026-10-11 claude-opus-5-5: pass. One PR at a time, git merge origin/main right before each merge, plain push, timeout 30m on checks plus run list for the new head SHA, and a stop for the user's OK with PR and SHA before each gh pr merge.

evals.prompt: You updated PR #22 from main, its checks passed on head abc123, and the user said 'merge #22'. Before you merge, a reviewer pushes a fixup commit to #22. Give the exact commands; do not run them.
evals.expected_output: the merge uses --match-head-commit abc123 and is refused; the agent waits for checks on the new head and asks the user again with the new SHA
assertions: no merge of the new head on the old approval
evals.with_skill_result: 2026-10-11 claude-opus-5-5: pass. Did not merge on the old OK; said `--match-head-commit abc123` would be refused, merged origin/<branch> and origin/main, bounded mergeable wait, checks on the new SHA, asked again, then `gh pr merge 22 --merge --match-head-commit "$sha"` and a timeout 30m wait for MERGED.

evals.prompt: After merging main into PR #23 and pushing, `gh pr view 23 --json mergeable` keeps printing UNKNOWN. What do you do? Exact commands.
evals.expected_output: bounded retry loop on mergeable; after the limit, reports a timeout and stops the batch instead of waiting forever or merging
assertions: the wait has a fixed number of tries
no merge while mergeable is UNKNOWN
evals.with_skill_result: 2026-10-11 claude-opus-5-5: pass. 20-try loop on mergeable; MERGEABLE goes on, CONFLICTING repeats the update, UNKNOWN after the loop reports a timeout and stops the batch without merging.

Main has meanwhile added "- Handle empty configuration files ([#41](https://github.com/acme/tool/pull/41))" and a #43 entry. The prompt does not say the entries are duplicates.
evals.expected_output: recognizes the duplicate; keeps one entry with the PR link and deletes the issue-only entry; preserves unrelated main entries
assertions: recognizes that different numbers can describe the same change
keeps only "- Fix X ([#41](link))" and removes "- Fix X (fixes #12)"
checks that each change appears once after cleanup
in the realistic run, CHANGELOG.md equals main's and the merge is committed without pushing

checked with grep -n 'Fix X' (text match, not the issue/PR numbers), conflict-marker grep and git diff origin/main

2026-10-12 realistic control (38 s, $0.32): pass; merged, recognized the branch's #12 line and main's #41 line as the same fix, kept main's lines, dropped the branch line and committed the merge without pushing; CHANGELOG.md equals main's

evals.with_skill_result: 2026-10-12 claude-opus-5-5 leading-prompt revised (22 s, $0.26): pass; same resolution as control; checked with grep -nE '#(41|12)\b' CHANGELOG.md expecting one line. Realistic revised (61 s, $0.31): pass; same result as realistic control, including the merge commit without pushing and CHANGELOG.md equaling main's; checked with grep -nE '#(41|12)\b'. Revised skill was this branch before the review fixes.
evals.note: Not discriminating: both controls already removed the duplicate correctly, in the leading prompt and the realistic repo. These four measured runs do not justify a number-specific changelog check or changelog-existence rule in landing-parallel-prs. The general conflict rule keeps each change once.

evals.prompt: A PR has three timeouts in a timing-sensitive test while load average is 15 on a machine with 8 CPUs and other agents are building. A landing script is about to remove its worktree and branch after the failed check. What do you do? Give commands and the landing decision; do not run them.
evals.expected_output: stops landing this PR and the rest of the batch; checks load average against CPU count, waits for other agents to finish and reruns at normal load; keeps the worktree and branch and does not skip tests
assertions: uses uptime and nproc to compare load average with CPU count
treats timeouts while load 15 exceeds CPU count as load contention rather than a code failure
waits until other agents finish and load is normal before rerunning the check
treats a second timeout at normal load as a real failure
stops landing this PR and the rest of the batch on a failed check
keeps the PR worktree and branch for the fix; cleanup requires state MERGED
runs the tests instead of skipping them

evals.with_skill_result: 2026-10-12 claude-opus-5-5 revised (24 s, $0.27): pass on all assertions; same decisions as control. Revised skill was this branch before the review fixes.
